name: Boerperd
notes: The SA Boerperd - a Cape-derived farmer's horse. Broad in solid colour: bay, brown, black, chestnut, buckskin, palomino, smoky black, grey, roan and rare dun, with flaxen and rabicano as modifiers.
Solid-bodied by breed standard, which requires pigmented skin and rejects pinto-like marking - so tobiano, frame, splash, sabino and the W series are all absent.
Most are naturally five-gaited, with a rack or amble on top of the ordinary gaits. DMRT3 carries the gait allele, but gait itself is not modelled - see the roadmap.
All disorders clear: the breed has a performance-trait study but no carrier rates for this panel.
The distinction between SA Boerperd and Cape Boerperd is not modelled.

A double-cream foal is barred from registration, and breeders are warned off mating two cream dilutes. Cream is kept where it is - high enough for buckskin, palomino and smoky black, low enough that a double dilute is an uncommon founder - and the pair stays reachable by breeding, because it is a registry rule rather than a disorder. The same shape as the Chilean Corralero.

Traced to the Cape settlement after 1652, from Barb and Arabian-type horses imported by way of Java, and rebuilt from remote survivors after heavy losses in the Anglo-Boer wars. Mares must stand at least 13.3 hh and stallions at least 14.2 hh; the band here starts at 14.2 hh, so it is the stallion minimum that sets the floor and the smallest registrable mares fall below anything this breed rolls.
Black pigmented skin is required by the standard, which is the other half of why no white pattern is named here.
